learning_outcomes.text: Student has ordered and theoretically supported knowledge about linear electrical circuits, their two-terminal and multi-terminal elements, and basic circuit properties.
Student knows mathematical methods useful in the analysis of DC and sinusoidally varying steady-state electrical circuits (symbolic method).
Student can use learned methods to analyze DC and sinusoidally varying steady-state electrical systems.
Student can choose the appropriate circuit analysis method and justify this choice.
Student can determine the responses of electrical circuits in steady-state DC and sinusoidally varying conditions.
Student understands the need for continuous self-improvement and raising their professional competencies.
Student is aware of the responsibility to act professionally and adhere to professional ethics.

syllabus_topics: Auditorium classes are conducted in accordance with the lecture topics.

Basic concepts of circuit theory. Two-terminal and multi-terminal elements of electrical circuits. R, L, C elements; current-voltage relationships, power and energy. Linear and nonlinear elements. Independent and controlled sources. Coupled inductances. Ideal transformer. Operational amplifier. Gyrator. Circuit equations. Kirchhoff's laws. Analysis of linear circuits in steady-state with constant excitation. Superposition principle. Thevenin's and Norton's theorems. Compensation theorem. Reciprocity principle. Mesh current method. Nodal potential method. Power in DC circuits. Matching receiver to source. Analysis of resistive circuits with operational amplifiers. Circuit topology/structure. Application of graph theory to electrical circuit analysis. Matrices describing electrical circuits: nodal matrix, loop matrix. Graph tree, fundamental loops and cut-sets. Analysis of linear circuits in steady-state with sinusoidal excitation. Complex amplitude method. Impedance and admittance of a two-port network. Equivalent diagrams of elements in the complex amplitude method. Vector diagrams of complex amplitudes. Power in sinusoidally varying current circuits: instantaneous, active, reactive, apparent, symbolic power. Matching receiver to source. Power factor of a two-port network. Reactive power compensation. Series and parallel resonant circuits. Parameters of resonant circuits. Fourier series. Spectrum of periodic signals. Analysis of linear electrical circuits with periodic excitations in steady-state. Power in electrical circuits with periodic excitations. Parseval's theorem.
teaching_methods: Practice method (doing tasks at the blackboard)
assessment_rules: Lectures are assessed by passing the exam. Auditorium classes are assessed based on presence, activity, and a positive grade from written or oral colloquia, which contributes to the final grade for this form of classes.
